entities.name: Query epsin-like protein
observations: 768 aa soluble, acidic protein with theoretical pI 5.41 and no reported transmembrane segment in the sequence analysis.
Contains a high-confidence N-terminal ENTH domain at residues 26–148; an overlapping ANTH-domain match is weaker and likely reflects shared structural homology.
C-terminal half is rich in proline, glutamine, serine, glycine, and asparagine, consistent with intrinsically disordered interaction and regulatory regions.
Sequence homology supports the epsin family, especially human EPSIN2 (O95208; 35.7% identity, 81.1% query coverage) and EPSIN3 (Q9H201; 34.9% identity, 86.2% query coverage).

entities.name: EPSIN2
observations: Reviewed human epsin-2 is involved in formation of clathrin-coated invaginations and endocytosis.
Annotated to cytoplasm, cytosol, cytoplasmic vesicles, and clathrin-coated vesicles, with concentration near the Golgi.
Binds AP-2 and clathrin and interacts with EPS15 and ITSN1; annotated for phospholipid binding and endocytosis.

entities.name: EPSIN3
observations: Reviewed human epsin-3 is associated with clathrin-coated pits and vesicles, the cytoplasmic side of the plasma membrane, and sometimes the nucleus.
Annotated for phospholipid binding, EH-domain binding, and endocytosis.

entities.name: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis
observations: Epsin homologs participate in clathrin-coated pit and vesicle formation and endocytosis through membrane phospholipid binding and interactions with clathrin-associated proteins.
